3
A hollow cylinder, which is open at both ends, has a radius of (3.0 ± 0.1) cm and a length of
(15.0 ± 0.1) cm.
What is the value, with its absolute uncertainty, of the surface area of the cylinder?
A
(280 ± 10) cm2
B
(282.7 ± 0.2) cm2
C
(420 ± 30) cm2
D
(424.1 ± 0.3) cm2

hints: Notice the cylinder is hollow and open at both ends, so the surface area is only the curved area $A = 2\pi r l$ with $r = 3.0 \text{ cm}$ and $l = 15.0 \text{ cm}$.
For a product, add the fractional uncertainties: $\Delta r / r = 0.1/3.0$ and $\Delta l / l = 0.1/15.0$, with the constant $2\pi$ having no uncertainty.
Multiply the total fractional uncertainty by the calculated area $2\pi \times 3.0 \times 15.0$ to get the absolute uncertainty, then round value and uncertainty to a sensible precision.
walkthrough: The open ends contribute no area, so use the curved surface $A = 2\pi r l$ with $r = 3.0 \text{ cm}$ and $l = 15.0 \text{ cm}$.
Calculate fractional uncertainties: for radius $0.1/3.0 \approx 0.0333$ or $3.33\%$, and for length $0.1/15.0 \approx 0.00667$ or $0.67\%$.
Add for multiplication: total fractional uncertainty $\approx 0.0333 + 0.00667 = 0.040$, so absolute uncertainty $\Delta A \approx 0.040 \times 282.7 \approx 11.3 \text{ cm}^2$.
Round to matching precision as $280 \text{ cm}^2$ with $\pm 10 \text{ cm}^2$, keeping only one significant figure in the uncertainty. This is option A.

A.explanation: Curved area $2\pi r l \approx 283 \text{ cm}^2$ with about $4\%$ fractional uncertainty gives about $11 \text{ cm}^2$, correctly rounded to $(280 \pm 10) \text{ cm}^2$.

B.explanation: Value $282.7 \text{ cm}^2$ is correct but $\pm 0.2 \text{ cm}^2$ just adds the absolute uncertainties $0.1+0.1$, which is wrong for a multiplied quantity.

C.explanation: About $420 \text{ cm}^2$ is too large and comes from using diameter instead of radius or adding end areas for a cylinder that is open at both ends.

D.explanation: Value $424.1 \text{ cm}^2$ is too large and $\pm 0.3 \text{ cm}^2$ wrongly combines absolute uncertainties instead of fractional uncertainties in $2\pi r l$.
